# MiniMax Launches M3.1 Flash — Claims 3x Faster Inference and 70% Lower Cost

> **In short:** MiniMax officially rolled out M3.1 Flash today, claiming the model is nearly three times faster at online inference and 70% cheaper to run, with the biggest gains in coding, agent, and cybersecurity tasks. For everyday users, the practical effect could be that AI tools you already use get faster and cheaper in the coming months.

A new AI model just dropped, and MiniMax is making some big promises about it. M3.1 Flash is the company's latest "Flash" model — a category that usually means the faster, lighter cousin of a full-sized AI. Think of it like the difference between a phone's battery-saver mode and its high-performance mode.

## What MiniMax says it does better

According to the announcement, M3.1 Flash delivers a "generational leap" in four specific areas. Here's each one in plain English.

- **Agentic tasks.** An "agent" is an AI that can take actions on its own — like opening a browser, clicking buttons, or filling in a form — instead of just answering questions. MiniMax says M3.1 Flash handles this multi-step work much better.
- **Coding.** AI that writes or fixes software. According to MiniMax, this model is a noticeable step up for code-related tasks.
- **Computer Use.** A specific AI skill where the model looks at a screen and controls a computer the way a person would — moving the cursor, opening apps, typing. MiniMax claims stronger performance here too.
- **Cybersecurity.** Tasks related to finding or fixing security problems in software.

## The speed and cost story

The two numbers MiniMax highlights most are about efficiency, not raw intelligence.

- **Online inference** — which just means "the moment the AI is actively processing your request" — is "nearly three times faster" than before, the company says.
- **Usage costs are cut by 70%**, also per MiniMax's own claim.

These are the company's own figures, not independent benchmarks. M3.1 Flash is rolling out today, so it will take time before outside reviewers can verify how those numbers hold up in the real world.

## What this means for you

- **If you use AI tools at work:** the apps and services your team pays for could get noticeably snappier, and per-request costs may drop. That matters most if your group relies on AI heavily — for example, summarizing long documents, drafting emails, or generating code.
- **If you use AI for personal tasks:** the chat assistants, writing helpers, and image tools on your phone might respond faster over time, especially as the apps get updated to run on newer, cheaper models in the background. You probably won't notice the model swap directly — you'll just notice the app feels quicker.
- **If you're new to AI:** you don't need to do anything today. M3.1 Flash is an upgrade happening behind the scenes. The most useful thing you can do right now is keep using whatever AI tool you already like, and treat unusually fast or cheap new features as a welcome surprise rather than something to chase.

The announcement today is mostly a story for developers and the companies building AI products. For the rest of us, the practical effect is simple: cheaper, faster AI is on the way, and the tools we use every day are likely to feel the benefits before we ever see the name "M3.1 Flash" out in the wild.
